question: DIGIPIN, an open-source nationwide geo-coded addressing system, is an alphanumeric code of how many characters based on latitude and longitude coordinates?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**10 characters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DIGIPIN** is an **open-source nationwide geo-coded addressing system** designed to create a standardized addressing mechanism.
 
• The system uses an **alphanumeric code consisting of 10 characters** based on **latitude and longitude coordinates**.
 
• The **latitude and longitude data** are used to precisely identify any location in a country, making it highly useful for **postal services, delivery systems, and geographical mapping.**
 
• This **10-character code** ensures accuracy and ease of use, eliminating the need for complex addresses.
 
• The system is especially beneficial in rural areas where proper addresses may not exist, as it provides a **standardized digital address system.**
 
• It can be integrated with various **navigation and mapping platforms** to enhance location-based services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Importance of DIGIPIN**__

 __
 
• The **10-character code** allows for precise and unique identification of locations across the country.
 
• This is an **open-source system**, meaning it is accessible to the public and can be adapted for various applications.
 
• It reduces confusion in **logistics and delivery services**, especially in areas with ambiguous or missing addresses.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of the Incorrect Options**__
 
 
• The other options, such as **6 characters, 8 characters, or 12 characters**, do not align with the standardized format of DIGIPIN, which is precisely 10 characters long.
 
• These options may represent hypothetical or alternative formats, but they are not applicable to DIGIPIN.
